China launched a dummy-warhead ballistic missile from a nuclear-powered submarine into the South Pacific, drawing immediate criticism from Australia, Japan, and New Zealand regarding regional security.

The Bright Side:
This test, while provocative, used a dummy warhead, avoiding immediate kinetic escalation or radioactive contamination of the zone.

The Breakdown & Plane Error:
This is a WHAT vs WHY error. They define the action as 'routine' (WHAT) while ignoring the geopolitical intent (WHY) to undermine regional defense pacts.

Social Physics Analysis:
Beijing uses the pretext of 'routine training' to mask a power play. By projecting military strength during a regional treaty signing, they attempt to intimidate neighbors while claiming innocence.

The Trajectory: The Path of Deception.
When you map the gap between stated intentions and ground-level results, it plots a direct trajectory toward Lesser Evil. The force of the action contradicts the stated peaceful intent.

The Unavoidable Truth: China is asserting its superpower status through military signaling.

The Unavoidable Lie: The test was a routine, non-targeted event without geopolitical intent.

Transparency is the bedrock of stability. By acting in the shadows of a nuclear-free zone, Beijing erodes the trust required for regional peace. This is a calculated move to test the limits of international norms.
